key_insight: The interaction of two drop-generated vortex rings depends strongly on the impact delay Δt, transitioning from symmetric merging to asymmetric or absent merging, and finally to independent evolution as the drops become sufficiently unsynchronized.
engineering_relevance: For flow control and mixing applications, precise timing of neighboring drop impacts is critical because small delays can fundamentally change vortex-ring formation and the resulting transport behavior.
method: Two water drops were released onto a deep water pool with controlled time differences Δt.
Particle image velocimetry was used to track the time evolution of the resulting vortex rings.
The interaction regimes were classified across a range of Δt values from sub-millisecond to tens of milliseconds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports four distinct vortex-ring evolution regimes identified from experiments, with thresholds at Δt < 0.5 ms, 0.5–7 ms, 7–80 ms, and Δt ≥ 80 ms.
watch_item: The reported regime boundaries are likely sensitive to drop size, impact conditions, and fluid properties, so they may not transfer directly to other liquids or geometries without revalidation.
paper_title: Interaction of vortex rings generated by two unsynchronised drop impacts
